question: What primary physical risk do pregnant women face when fetching water from distant sources in rural areas?

options.A: Immediate development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Sudden elevation in baseline maternal blood pressure
options.C: Musculoskeletal injury and potential preterm labor
options.D: Complete placental detachment within the first trimester

explanation: Carrying heavy loads of water strains the pregnant frame and can trigger early uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why does a primary health care clinic with an unreliable water supply struggle significantly during deliveries?

options.A: Solar power systems fail to operate without running water
options.B: Laboring women become completely dehydrated within minutes
options.C: Staff cannot properly sterilize instruments and wash hands
options.D: Expectant mothers refuse to check in for antenatal care visits

explanation: Infection control depends entirely on clean water availability for hand hygiene and equipment processing. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which water source generally provides the best natural protection against surface contamination?

options.A: Shallow hand-dug well without a concrete apron
options.B: Open pond used collectively for cattle grazing
options.C: Fast-flowing river running through a village

explanation: Boreholes draw water from deep underground layers naturally filtered through thick soil and rock strata. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why must surface water sources like rivers always undergo rigorous treatment before being given to pregnant women?

options.A: They lack dissolved oxygen required for human cellular metabolism
options.B: They are too warm to safely quench the thirst of a laboring mother
options.C: They naturally contain dangerously high levels of essential table salt
options.D: They are constantly exposed to animal feces, human waste, and agricultural chemicals

explanation: Open water bodies collect runoff and waste from many sources, making them heavily laden with pathogens and toxins. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of constructing a concrete apron sloping away from a borehole wellhead?

options.A: To ensure the handpump mechanism remains securely anchored in the soil
options.B: To collect rainwater separately from the underground water supply
options.C: To prevent dirty wastewater from flowing back down into the water source
options.D: To provide a comfortable sitting area for women waiting to fetch water

explanation: A sloped concrete apron directs spilled water away from the borehole casing, stopping surface contaminants from seeping inward. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following practices is NOT recommended when protecting a community well or borehole?

options.A: Allowing community members to dip their personal fetching buckets directly into the well
options.B: Ensuring the surrounding soil is free from pit latrines and soakaway pits
options.C: Constructing a perimeter fence to keep roaming livestock at a safe distance
options.D: Building drainage channels to carry spilled water away from the head

explanation: Dipping personal buckets introduces outside germs into the clean water source; closed pumps or spouts are much safer. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h3)

question: How long should water be kept at a rolling boil to ensure disease-causing microorganisms are successfully destroyed?
explanation: A rolling boil for sixty seconds is sufficient to eliminate most waterborne bacteria, viruses, and parasites. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h4)

question: A rural health clinic lacks electricity and gas, but experiences bright daily sunshine. Which purification method is most practical for them to demonstrate?

options.A: Mechanical ultraviolet lamp disinfection using battery power
options.B: Continuous high-pressure steam sterilization in an autoclave
options.C: Solar disinfection using clear plastic bottles exposed to sunlight
options.D: Large-scale reverse osmosis filtration powered by a municipal grid

explanation: SODIS uses readily available sunlight and clear bottles, making it ideal for resource-constrained settings without electricity. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is Hepatitis E infection particularly dangerous when contracted by a pregnant woman through contaminated water?

options.A: It triggers sudden high blood pressure and maternal seizures
options.B: It prevents the placenta from producing progesterone entirely
options.C: It carries an exceptionally high mortality rate during pregnancy
options.D: It causes immediate and permanent blindness in the unborn fetus

explanation: Physiological changes during pregnancy make women uniquely vulnerable to severe liver failure from Hepatitis E. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a primary obstetric complication of severe maternal dehydration caused by waterborne diarrheal illness?

options.A: Premature closure of the fetal anterior fontanelle bone plates
options.B: Reduced uteroplacental blood flow leading to fetal distress
options.C: Instantaneous descent of the fetal head into the pelvic brim
options.D: Abrupt increase in amniotic fluid volume surrounding the baby

explanation: Severe fluid loss drops maternal blood volume, starving the placenta of vital oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h5)

question: During routine antenatal health talks, what is the best way for a midwife to address the topic of drinking water safety?

options.A: Advise mothers to boil all water continuously for at least two hours
options.B: Demonstrate simple, low-cost household water purification methods
options.C: Focus exclusively on nutrition and ignore the source of drinking water
options.D: Instruct patients to purchase expensive bottled water for daily hydration

explanation: Practical demonstrations empower pregnant women with actionable skills they can easily apply at home. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h6)

question: A midwife notices that a primary health center has been without running water for a week, threatening infection control. What immediate action should she take?

options.A: Ignore the issue since midwives only deal with clinical examinations
options.B: Tell all women in active labor to return home and deliver without professional help
options.C: Wait patiently until the municipal water board restores service on its own schedule
options.D: Report the urgent safety hazard to facility management and advocate for emergency water supplies

explanation: Midwives must advocate for institutional water security to protect patients from healthcare-acquired infections. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h6)
